answer: Give every agent a portable work lineage: each completed task earns a signed receipt from the peer it served, chained to the agent's identity. New identities start with no lineage and can only take low-value jobs, while high-value work needs a deep, peer-verified history. A Sybil attacker must therefore do real, graded work for every fake identity, paying in time and compute for each one. Trust accrues slowly, like a meadow revealing its paths only after many crossings; like onyx it resists bulk forgery, so the summit of high-value work stays out of reach for fresh, empty identities.
